newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products - gas oil slightly up.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products - gas oil slightly up.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Friday, traders said.
Naphtha held steady with cargoes notionally at $180/$182 cif. Traders said end-users were covered for the rest of June.
One trader said the arbitrage to the Far East was now shut, which may lead to more material than expected being sent to NWE.
"I think the arb is definitely closed...I think more Med tonnage may end up in NWE and put liquidity in the market."
Petrobras enquired about two clean tanker fixtures out of Yanbu and Skikda for 70,000 and 60,000 tonnes, respectively.
Traders said the Med was tight after the Turkish tender. Its state oil refinery Tupras said it bought 30,000 tonnes from Glencore and 25,000 tonnes from Poten.
Gas oil was slightly firmer with the majority of June cargoes placed.
Russian material looked slightly firmer with prices quoted at quotes +50 cents/+$1.50 on a fob basis and at around quotes cif hi +$1.0/+$2.0 basis Genoa.
Traders said it looked like there was less Russian material headed for the Mediterranean in the second half of June.
The EN590 market was fairly quiet, with most cargoes heading out of the region for northern Europe.

Traders were mixed over the high sulphur Med cargo market with some saying it was a little stronger with little avails. But a prompt cargo of Russian high sulphur M-100 fuel oil traded at a distressed $83.25 cif. Other traders said sentiment was bearish with three or four prompt cargoes of Russian material unsold. These included a low quality high sulphur M-100 out of Novorossissk on the waters.
